issues.description: Test 'fix' weakens the assertion by injecting a zero-amount dummy addition to bypass __post_init__
issues.detail: The tests previously passed additions=[] to exercise the legacy single-recipient path. After the refactor, CreateSignedTransaction.__post_init__ requires len(self.additions) >= 1, so the tests now pass [Addition(amount=uint64(0), puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)] purely to satisfy the precondition. This is not a tested behavior — it is a smuggled stub addition with amount 0 to a zero puzzle hash. Either the new path silently strips/ignores zero-amount additions (in which case it is untested and unspecified), or it generates a coin to the zero address (in which case it is wrong). The test must state what it is verifying; right now it verifies nothing about that addition. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: cat_spend bypasses CATWallet's MAX_COIN_AMOUNT validation on additions
issues.detail: The old cat_spend body explicitly checked 'if addition.amount > MAX_COIN_AMOUNT: raise ValueError'. That precondition check is absent from the new forwarding code. If create_signed_transaction does not enforce the same bound on CAT additions, this is a silent loss of a stated precondition. The author has not demonstrated that the postcondition (rejection of out-of-range amounts) is preserved by the new control flow. State the invariant or restore the guard.

issues.description: cat_spend forwards inner_address through XCH-only address validation, but a CAT inner_address is not necessarily an XCH-prefixed bech32 string
issues.detail: ensure_valid_address(..., allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}, ...) is applied to request.inner_address in the CAT path. The old code did decode_puzzle_hash(request.inner_address) with no prefix check at all. Tightening this to XCH-only is a behavior change that is neither stated in the PR description nor justified by a stated specification. Either this is a correctness regression for legitimate non-XCH-prefix inner addresses, or it is a deliberate restriction that must be documented and tested. State the precondition explicitly.

issues.description: send_transaction silently drops the 'Unexpected Address Prefix' specific error for a generic ensure_valid_address failure
issues.detail: The old send_transaction raised ValueError('Unexpected Address Prefix') after a precise prefix comparison. The new code delegates to ensure_valid_address, which raises a differently-worded error. This changes the externally observable behavior of a public RPC endpoint. If clients pattern-match on error strings (and given this is a JSON-RPC surface, some do), they will break. Either preserve the message or document the contract change.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation: control flow disguises a smuggled goto via 'None in {set}' on a set containing None and strings
issues.detail: The condition 'None in {extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution}' constructs a set whose membership semantics depend on hashability and equality of heterogeneous types (str, bytes, NoneType). It happens to work, but the reader cannot evaluate correctness without simulating the set construction. A clearer formulation is the explicit 'any(x is None for x in (...))'. More importantly: the branch structure (None-and-None-and-None vs. None-in-set vs. else) is three disjoint predicates expressed as if/elif/else, which makes the reader prove the partition is exhaustive and disjoint. State the invariant: 'exactly all-None or all-non-None'. The type: ignore comments are the smell — mypy cannot follow the reasoning because the reasoning is not in the code.

issues.description: Two classes silently share validation by duplicated CAT-discrepancy fields rather than composition
issues.detail: CATSpend and CreateSignedTransaction now both carry extra_delta/tail_reveal/tail_solution and both expose a cat_discrepancy property delegating to the same free function. This is duplication-by-copy of a precondition. The structured approach is to introduce a CATDiscrepancy value object whose __post_init__ enforces the invariant once, and embed it. As written, two request schemas can drift apart, and the 'cat specific' comment is the only thing tying them together. Manage complexity in one place.

issues.description: 'opportunity to raise' comment is a load-bearing side effect with no postcondition
issues.detail: Both refactored handlers call self.service.wallet_state_manager.get_wallet(...) purely for its raising side effect and discard the result. The comment '# opportunity to raise' is folklore in place of specification. State the precondition: 'wallet_id refers to a wallet of type Wallet/CATWallet'. Then either (a) pass the validated wallet object through, or (b) factor out a require_wallet_type(...) helper whose name states the precondition. A discarded function call relying on its exception behavior is exactly the kind of smuggled control flow that structured programming exists to prevent.

issues.description: Addition positional construction relies on field order with no keyword arguments
issues.detail: Both new call sites construct Addition(request.amount, decode_puzzle_hash(...), request.memos) positionally. The Addition class has fields amount, puzzle_hash, memos in some order in a Streamable dataclass — and the codebase's convention elsewhere appears to use keyword arguments. Positional construction here makes the call sites silently dependent on declaration order, and any reordering of Addition fields would silently miscompile. Use kw_only/keyword args.

issues.description: Comment 'Curious that mypy doesn't see the elif' is left in the extracted function — folklore preserved verbatim
issues.detail: The remark, charming as it is, documents the author's surprise at a tool rather than the function's specification. The type: ignore comments are a confession that the code's structure does not let the type-checker (or a reader) prove the invariant. Restructuring to e.g. matching a tuple pattern or constructing an Optional NamedTuple removes the ignores. Either fix the reasoning so the ignores go away, or document the invariant the ignores rest on. Don't preserve a confused comment by copy-paste.

issues.description: json_serialize_for_transport round-trip from a typed request through JSON and back is an unstated invariant
issues.detail: Both forwarders build a CreateSignedTransaction, then call .json_serialize_for_transport(...) and pass the result back into self.create_signed_transaction(...), which presumably deserializes it again. The postcondition of this round-trip — that no field is lost, no type is coerced, no default is silently re-applied — is unstated. For a refactor whose stated goal is 'simpler endpoints forward to richer ones', a direct in-process call would preserve types; the serialize/deserialize hop is friction that must be justified or removed.

issues.description: puzzle_decorator type relaxed to 'Clawback only' via comment, not via type system
issues.detail: The comment 'Technically this value was meant to support many types... as a slight hack, we'll specify that only Clawback is supported' admits the type does not state the design intent. If only Clawback is supported, the field type should be 'list[ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride]' (already is) and the comment should state why no abstraction is provided. If extension is anticipated, an abstract base or Union should be declared now. 'Slight hack' is not a specification.

review.summary: This PR is a deduplication refactor in the right direction — collapsing two endpoints into a richer one is structurally sound — but the execution leaks unstated preconditions in several places. The test change from additions=[] to additions=[Addition(amount=uint64(0), puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)] is the most damning: it exists to satisfy a __post_init__ assertion rather than to verify behavior, which is TESTED-NOT-PROVED in its purest form. A MAX_COIN_AMOUNT check has gone missing from the CAT path; an XCH-only address restriction has appeared without specification on a CAT endpoint; a discarded get_wallet call is doing load-bearing exception work behind a folklore comment. The extracted cat_discrepancy_validation is duplicated across two request classes rather than composed, and its 'None in {set}' construction with three type: ignore admits the invariant is not expressed in the code. REASONED in intent, UNREASONED in detail. Refuse until preconditions and postconditions are restated and the tests verify something.
